errata_items.finding: Historical report claimed XGBoost significantly outperformed Median and Zero-delay baselines across all point metrics.
errata_items.reconciliation: Empirical re-evaluation proves XGBoost outperforms baselines on RMSE (43.00m vs 45.76m) and Tail MAE >= 60m (117.18m vs 132.54m), but underperforms the trivial Median baseline on overall MAE (17.60m vs 15.60m). This is mathematically expected for an asymmetric zero-inflated delay distribution trained with an MSE objective pulling predictions to conditional expectation.

errata_items.finding: Historical artifact departure_probabilistic_readiness_v1.json claimed NGBoost Student-T achieved superior CRPS.
errata_items.reconciliation: Numerical audit shows Empirical Residual achieves CRPS of 10.20m, which is strictly lower (better) than NGBoost Student-T (14.23m). The claim that Student-T is 'superior by CRPS' was factually contradictory. Student-T is justified not by lowest CRPS, but by continuous parametric density modeling, heteroscedastic scale estimation (sigma(x)), and continuous log-likelihood (NLL=4.18).

errata_items.finding: Conflation between Point Champion, Probabilistic Marginal Champion, and Downstream Simulation Candidate.
errata_items.reconciliation: Formally decoupled into three independent roles: Role A (Point Champion: Ridge / Ensemble), Role B (Probabilistic Forecast Champion: P5 Quantile / Empirical for pinball/CRPS), and Role C (Downstream Simulation Candidate: P4 Student-T for continuous likelihood and stochastic sampling).

decision_summary: All reported metrics and model selection statements are reconciled with row-level data evidence.
